sections.title: Why trust me with it.
sections.intro: This isn't a sketch of how it might work. It's how I run a live Shopify build today.

items.claim: A biotech supplier's whole store, built from nothing
items.proof: Design system, customer personas, a custom theme and a catalogue manager for STR Technologies, a vaccine-adjuvant supplier selling to research buyers. Live as a prototype.
Products come from a single sheet through an admin layer with a Draft-to-Live step, so the person managing them never touches Shopify's raw backend and nothing goes live by accident.
Pricing, documents and checkout stay hidden until Shopify confirms a buyer as an approved business. Every deploy needs a version tag, closer to a software release than a theme tweak.

items.claim: I've built and sold my own product brand
items.proof: OGANIKO Raw Spanish Mountain Honey: I researched the niche and the buyer, built the brand, the packaging and the listings, and sold it on Allegro and Amazon. Before design, I imported and sold goods at London markets.

items.q: Why not just buy a theme?
items.a: I started that way: my first Shopify build used a premium theme that cost nearly $500. I've since found it faster and cheaper to build a static prototype from scratch, agree it with you, then build it into Shopify through its API and the Shopify CLI. That's far more flexible than bending a theme: you get what your shop needs, and nothing more.

items.q: Can you take over an existing Shopify store?
items.a: Often, yes. I start by mapping the catalogue, the apps and what your team actually edits, then decide what to keep.

items.q: Do you work with business buyers?
items.a: Yes. Approved accounts, their own price lists, documents and payment terms are part of how I build.

items.q: Can the shop sell in more than one language?
items.a: Yes. I work in English, German, French and Polish, and plan the catalogue for every language from the start.
